head: 30b63a25131f910d07d884b425a69c8ad782faef
review_scope: Complete two-file diff; all five changed closures, enclosing unread/consume flow, commit/cursor ordering, existing locked source-validation selector, Range select/unread/cut code and demand-driven digest/codec owners. Relevant pool cancellation/nesting and lane/purge writer contracts inspected. Not every unchanged Consumer function or all Memory authority code.

delta_assessment.change: Only wrap existing expressions in Domain_pool_ref.submit_cpu_or_inline ~name:__FUNCTION__; callers await each result in the same control-flow order. No Range/window algorithm, prefilter, extent, argument, match arm, cache or digest memo change. MLI adds bounded placement/authority documentation only.
delta_assessment.remaining_work: Other pure operations including prefilters, witness checks and Capture.project_source remain where they already ran; this is not a claim that all Librarian CPU has moved.

immutability_and_digest.inputs: trace_id strings, read boundary/result lists, progress records, range records and decoded checkpoint message lists are immutable values. exact_snapshot_messages is a plain snapshot.checkpoint.messages projection; closure retains its value rather than reloading storage. Agent-Core base messages instantiate immutable provider record/variant constructors with History media refs; no Eio resource, channel, store capability or mutable shared digest accumulator is captured by these five closures.
immutability_and_digest.locality: Window.annotate allocates local labels; atom_opening_index/atom_opening_digest build their own local opener array and lookup closure inside the worker call. This is demand-driven lookup, not shared Lazy.t state. No lookup closure/array escapes in Range results; different jobs share only immutable message values.
immutability_and_digest.order: Unchanged selector filters/refusals and calls digest_at in the original order. Each requested opener still goes through Checkpoint.message_to_json, Yojson.Safe.to_string and SHA256 with no eager prehash, cross-call memo or new query short-circuit. Completed noncancelled work has the same returned result/writer failure path; cancellation may prevent an entire queued job from evaluating.

codec_purity.chain: Checkpoint.message_to_json -> Checkpoint_codec.message_to_json -> History.message_to_json; recursive text/tool blocks delegate to Api_common wire helpers.
codec_purity.media: History.Stored writes sha256/byte-count metadata directly; Url/File_id are encoded as existing strings. These encoding functions do not invoke History media-store resolve/to_wire, open files or fetch URLs. Text UTF8 repair is a local string transformation; signature-bearing thinking keeps exact bytes. Unrelated TLS/media I/O helpers elsewhere in the modules are not called by this chain.
codec_purity.exceptions: No new catch, fallback/default, retry or writer-exception suppression. The existing pool contract re-raises job errors instead of rerunning them inline.

scheduling_and_cancellation.placement: With an installed selected pool and an ordinary Eio caller, shared CPU weight1 is used; Read lane chooses read pool. No pool or a raw non-Eio caller runs inline. Domain_pool marks worker fibers and inherited fibers; already-worker calls run inline before attempting another submission. This avoids queueing behind the same one-worker capacity.
scheduling_and_cancellation.nested_source_validation: The separate R.select in checkpoint_message_floor remains inside the existing submit_io_or_inline exact-snapshot/session-lock job. No new nested CPU submission or lock-order change was inserted there.
scheduling_and_cancellation.new_interleavings: Each new offload can suspend its caller before the pure result is available. Checkpoint/log/cursor files or runtime metadata can change meanwhile, but worker code reads the originally captured values and cannot mint freshness. Normal appends therefore do not mutate its input; no file read is moved into a CPU closure. Existing stale-observation and authority boundaries are not made atomic by this change.
scheduling_and_cancellation.side_effect_order: Five new jobs do not commit Memory, ACK external input or write progress. Their results still feed the existing selection/recovery/commit paths. Ordinary Memory revision capture/prepare/commit remains later; committed-prefix recovery retains its original earlier coverage observation and subsequent write path. No new freshness or replacement proof is claimed for that path.
scheduling_and_cancellation.cancel_settlement: Executor_pool_submission distinguishes Awaiting/Entered/Cancelled-before-entry, cancels worker scope and joins entered work under protection before re-raising caller cancellation. Pure OCaml work need not stop immediately if it reaches no cooperative cancellation point. It has no durable effects even if it finishes while cancellation is settling.
scheduling_and_cancellation.lane_discipline: Existing progress writer contract serializes normal Librarian work and cancels/joins it before purge. Keeper_memory_lane cancels all owned units before awaiting exits; worker settlement therefore precedes lane completion/purge action. The provisional failed-range marker remains set across raised exceptions/cancellation as before; existing protected cursor settlement is unchanged.
scheduling_and_cancellation.scope_limit: No new empirical one-worker, cancellation, concurrent append/replacement, purge or output-parity test was run. These are source/policy conclusions, not executed scenarios.

separate_memory_owner.boundary: 04fa Memory_replaced/selection-guard additions are not part of30b63a25, are not edited or approved here, and are not credited as an offload effect. Existing source/Memory authority behavior remains its own owner/review scope.

r1.failure: Actual missing public_cmi/masc__Keeper_memory_os_current.cmi stopped the first complete MLI compile; no candidate ML typing was reached. Original failed record retained.

r2.prefix: Same actual dependency/include/flags prefix as r1 after normalizing only the new output-leaf path. No fake signature, include workaround, warning suppression or -impl bypass.
r2.signature: Full same-basename MLI precedes -c full ML, fatal warnings4/8/32/69. This establishes complete Consumer source/interface typing against currently available real prebuilt CMIs. No before/after CMI-stability capture is claimed.
r2.limit: No native execution, full Dune/library wrapping validation, whole product build, functional suite or installed-runtime verification. Dependency CMI SHA is captured; exact source-build provenance of the broad shared graph remains unproved.

existing_ops_evidence.assessment: Existing PID64072 one-second availability sample contains Range/demand-digest frames; receipt explicitly says availability diagnosis, not comparative performance. It is a clue for choosing a placement change, not CPU share, total CPU reduction, latency recovery or a before/after baseline.

limits: No compiler, Dune, CI, native function test, runtime/profile/GC/restart, provider, GitHub or ref operation was performed by reviewer. R2 compile was performed by parent and independently inspected from retained source/argv/terminal logs.
Source placement may reduce caller-domain occupancy when a pool is installed; no controlled latency/throughput/totalCPU improvement is measured. Inline contexts keep the original execution placement.
Review is exact head/base/two-file scope; changed source or new base requires a bounded delta binding. This is not a formal GitHub approval or approval of unrelated Memory source fixes.
